findings.detail: Immediately tracked accepted-handler promises include queued before-hook work. Owned upstream-close, raw response/private retainer, after-exchange certification and original-error retention promises are tracked as well. Close repeats allSettled over the live set, including nested registrations, after transport closure; socket closure alone cannot imply completed handler/evidence.

All calls share the same closePromise while pending and after success/failure. Success requires real transport closure and sockets/forwarded/handlers/evidence/ownedWork/active all0 before closed=true. Existing10-second deadline retains actual outstanding counts and closed=false/incomplete; background settlement cannot later turn the timed-out receipt into success.

Original before/upstream/raw/after failures retain name/message/stack/code privately. The first original Error is propagated only after tracked retention settles; public lifecycle includes fixed category/hash references, not raw messages. Failed raw retention cannot invoke a false after-certificate. No generic success or synthetic zero replaces a timeout or failure.

Deadline force only destroys already-owned sockets/upstream requests. Original request method/path/headers/body/dispatch/status/raw bytes and business assertions remain. No new business retry, fixture ownership, producer permission, PG restore or process-kill authorization is added. Old uir3a partial/late records remain and sole actual cause is not asserted.
